# U.S. Inflation August 2026: Prices Rise 3.4% as Energy Jumps 16.3%

September 22, 2026 6 Min Read

 

The latest data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics shows that consumer prices increased 3.4% in the 12 months through August 2026. Prices rose another 0.4% in August alone, after increasing 0.1% in July.

The biggest increase came from energy, where prices were up 16.3% from a year earlier. Gasoline prices were 27.4% higher, while fuel oil prices increased 52.0%.

Food prices also continued to rise, although at a much slower pace. Food prices were up 2.7% over the year, while prices for food purchased at restaurants increased 3.4%.

- U.S. consumer prices rose 3.4% over the year through August 2026.
- Energy prices rose 16.3%, making energy the fastest-rising major category.

# Fed raises US inflation outlook while lowering unemployment forecasts

Core PCE inflation forecast for 2026 revised upward to 3.4%; unemployment rate projected to remain at 4.1% through 2029

Mucahithan Avcioglu

16 September 2026• Update: 16 September 2026

ISTANBUL

The US Federal Reserve raised its inflation forecasts for 2026 on Wednesday, while lowering unemployment projections, signaling persistent price pressures alongside a resilient labor market.

The median forecast for core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation was raised to 3.4% for 2026 from 3.3% in June, according to the Fed’s latest Summary of Economic Projections.

The core measure, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, is expected to ease to 2.5% in 2027, 2.2% in 2028 and 2% in 2029.

The headline PCE inflation forecast for 2026 was also lifted by 0.1 percentage point to 3.7%. Inflation is projected to fall to 2.3% in 2027, 2.1% in 2028 and reach the Fed’s 2% target in 2029.

# Core CPI Was 2.4%, Lowest Since 2021. The Fed Hiked Anyway. Here's Why

The Sept. 11 CPI report gave both sides ammunition: low annual core inflation, a hot monthly core print, and an energy shock in the headline. Hike odds went to about 90%.

Market Events By Serena Golsby, Chief Market Strategist Published September 19, 2026 Updated September 28, 2026 6 min read

CPI day is usually straightforward: hot means NQ down, cool means NQ up. The August 2026 report, released September 11, 2026, was harder to read, and how people read it says a lot about where this market is.

## What happened

- Headline CPI rose 0.4% in August and 3.4% year over year. That matched the consensus, according to FXStreet's analysis.
- Core CPI (excluding food and energy) rose 0.3% on the month, a tick hotter than expected, ending a three-month run of softer readings.
- Core CPI was up 2.4% over 12 months, per the BLS summary. US Inflation Calculator
